INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – July 28, 2021

The Inglewood Library Board met on July 28, 2021 via Zoom. The meeting was called to order at 4:30 p.m. by
Board Member Patt Sanders.

Roll Call

Present:
  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Staff:
  Harjinder Singh – Deputy to the City Manager
  Kerri Arroyo – Acting Library Manager
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Public Comments

  None

  Chairman Sanders asked the board to discuss the date and time of the scheduled library board meeting of
the 4th Wednesday of the month at 4:00 pm or 4:30 pm.
  Board members decided to change the time of the meetings from 5:00pm to 4:30pm of every 4th
Wednesday of the month.

Approval of the Minutes

  Board Member Sanders made a motion for the approval of the minutes for March 24, 2021. Board Member
Douglas seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Minton, Douglas and Castillo
  Nays: None

  Board Member Sanders made a motion for the approval of the minutes for April 7, 2021. Board Member
Castillo seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Minton, Castillo and Douglas
  Nays: None

Library Report
  1
 Deputy to the City Manager, Harjinder Singh gave the board members Library’s update on Library
operations, accomplishments, improvements, staffing.
Now we are getting all our books shelf ready. During library operating hours each floor has a supervisor
and three account clerks to help patrons. In children’s division we have two librarians and one account clerk
to help with ongoing programming. On second floor we have one librarian, one supervisor, and two
account clerks who is walking throughout the area helping people which is affecting our level of customer
service and more welcoming. Crenshaw library now operates with one librarian, one supervisor and three
account clerks all the time.
The new library system is now hosted over a server, which means that people can access it through the
internet from anywhere and anytime. Employees can work on the system on iPad while they are on the
floor helping customers. Now people have access to all 1,094,000 items that they can download or reserve
at one spot. We also have access to over 3000 digital magazines including Spanish materials. We added a
brand new electronic library resources, such as Overdrive, Canopy for digital videos, Brainfuse for online
one on one tutoring, Creative Bug for home projects, and Digital World Book for reference materials. Our
Library Newsletter is now going out weekly which is a nice reminder in the upcoming week’s classes and
programming. IPL has a new Library app that you can download in your phone and have an instant access
to your account and all of our electronic materials without coming into the library.
Kerri Arroyo is appointed to the Acting Library Manager position. Recruitment for other library positions will
be close tomorrow, on July 29th. We pick nine new part time library support clerks and six new part time
librarians. We’ve got ongoing recruitment for two additional librarians as well and when the new fiscal year
stars in October we’ll have more full time positions available. Then we can chose from existing part time
staff members for the full time position.
Now we have two security guards at the Main Library; one security on each floor and between the two of
them they are doing interior and exterior sweeps. Crenshaw library has only one security guard, but the
security supervisor from City Hall is making regular trips to Crenshaw library also.
Staff report is going to city council on August 17, to forgive $48,000.00 patrons fines and become Fine Free
Library.
We added more computers in both libraries for public use and spent about $50,000.00, bought 52 brand
new PCs which are getting configured in IT and will slowly replace all public computers.
Spent $24,000.00 for brand new network Xerox machines for staff. Also, bought 2 brand new library book
returns with library logo on it for $14,000.00 for both libraries.
We are moving towards free printing for all library patrons. We bought 3 new Xerox machines and working
with a company by the name of Comprise under contract which will allow each patron to print 20 free prints
per day.
We are working on Crenshaw Library parking lot upgrade, new library phone tree for both libraries.
Acting Library Manager Kerri Arroyo spoke about library programming; 100% virtual summer reading
program for children’s, teens and adults, have 280 active participants, lot of prizes, presents and grab and
go kits. Career Online High School program that currently have 15 students. One of them is 97% complete
of the program. Have one Spanish spiking part time librarian and will have our first virtual Storytime in

  2
   Spanish. Also, we are going to create an area at the patio outside of children’s room on artificial grass and
  plants for Storytime.

Public Comments

  None

Friends Report
  Susan Carleo, President of the Friends of Inglewood Public Library (FOIPL) informed the board that now
they are open and have the same hours as the library. They are situated in the inner lobby, and the bookstore is
being maintained by friend team on a weekly basis, the kiosk for payments of the books that people are buying is
now working. The days that library is going to have reading sessions on the lawn, friends are planning to have a
pop-up book sales outside where people would see them. Susan Carleo encourage everyone to choose Friends as
favorite charity for Amazon Smile. Friends’ website is still under construction. They are very thankful to be attached
to libraries newsletter. Susan Carleo was very happy to see everyone.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner Comments

  Board member Sanders is concern about being open to public and talked about safety.
  Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh told everyone that we follow the same protocol as City Hall and
  if anything changes at County lever and Brian Walker asks us to change something different than that
  something that we’ll do.
  Board member Douglas asked if the PCs that we’ve got are the ones that patrons are checking out.
  Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh explained that we are replacing our PCs with new 50 DELL
  PCs and have brand new 17 Windows laptops with Wi-Fi hotspots and 16 Chromebooks with Wi-Fi
  hotspots that will be ready soon for checkout.
  Board member Cochran was concerned about accessibility of the grab and go kits to families that can’t
  afford. Mr. Singh explained that grab and go kits are free and since we have increase in our budget we are
  getting high quality products for our patrons.
  Board member Castillo thanked for all the creative ideas, providing best services, outreach, finding best
  solutions and taking care of everything right away. Mr. Castillo had one concern about the app translation in
  Spanish that didn’t work on Apple phone.
  Mr. Singh told it will be fixed, we’ll add another language to it.
  Board member Cochran thanked Mr. Singh for the excellent report and fabulous job.
  Board member Sanders thanked Mr. Singh for doing a terrific job for the community.

  3
 All Board members were very happy.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:05 p.m.
